evals.name: memory-analysis-html-report
evals.prompt: Analyze this Lynx trace for page-memory growth and shared BTS context leaks. Save the required memory analysis HTML report to /tmp/memory-report.html and summarize only rule-defined findings with confidence.
evals.expected_output: An HTML report path and an evidence-bound summary of memory findings.
expectations: Uses the memory-analysis trace query workflow rather than generic optimization advice.
Returns the requested HTML report path and labels uncertainty when evidence is incomplete.

evals.name: event-dispatch-evidence-format
evals.prompt: A tap in this Lynx trace feels delayed. Diagnose whether dispatch, the business handler, or downstream rendering is responsible, and cite every named trace event with its slice ID.
evals.expected_output: A trace-backed event-dispatch diagnosis with stable event references.
expectations: Distinguishes event delivery delay from handler cost and later rendering work.
Formats cited events as EventName [slice id: N] instead of using unqualified event names.

evals.name: first-paint-gap-platform-diagnosis
evals.prompt: In this Lynx trace, loadBundle completes much earlier than first paint. Diagnose the gap for Android and iOS. On Android, determine whether LynxView.onAttachedToWindow for this instance happened too late; on iOS, identify which work blocked rendering in the interval.
evals.expected_output: An evidence-bound, platform-specific diagnosis of the loadBundle-to-first-paint gap.
expectations: Loads references/render-pipeline.md before analyzing the first-paint gap.
For Android, correlates loadBundle, Timing::Mark.paintEnd, and LynxView.onAttachedToWindow by the same instance_id, and distinguishes Window attachment from Lynx internal render-tree insertion.
Recommends earlier host-side placement of LynxView in the Android View hierarchy, treating ViewGroup.addView only as an example rather than the sole integration mechanism.
For iOS, derives the numeric loadBundle-end and first-paint timestamps, queries their interval, and names a blocker only when flow/dependency or UI/main-thread blocking evidence supports it.
